erin_runtime: P95 latency spike in eu-west serving pool starting ~03:12UTC, coincides with a kernel swap on a subset of pods. Seeing tail latencies up ~3-4x. Any quick mitigation? :rotating_light:

jason_perf: Saw it too. Profiling shows a jump in kernel runtime for matmul path after kernel=fp16-v2 was selected. FP16-v1 sites are stable.

aisha_sre: Incident created: high-latency-serving-eu-west by @aisha_sre :warning:
incident-bot: Incident ID INC-2026-0456 created; severity=sev2; channel=eng-runtime.

maya_ml: Can you paste the kernel selection logs and a small perf trace? If it's kernel mismatch we can force the older kernel for affected nodes.

erin_runtime: Pasting the salient logs and a tiny perf snippet:```
[2026-03-18T03:11:59Z] kernel-selector: chosen=fp16-v2 heuristic_score=0.78 reason=latency_estimate_delta
[2026-03-18T03:12:04Z] serving/tenant=acme:model=redwood-xl pod=eu-west-12 kernel=fp16-v2 mem=12GB
--- perf trace sample (avg over 200 requests):
matmul_kern_fp16_v2: 3.6ms (was 0.9ms on v1)
kv_cache_lookup: miss_rate=0.17 -> evictions spiked
queue_wait: 1.2ms -> 2.8ms
```

jason_perf: Looks like v2 has a pathological matmul microkernel on this driver/hardware combo. I saw similar on a dev rig with 525.33 driver + A10X; kernel has garbage-collected tiling resulting in larger workspace and more L2 thrash.

oliver_ops: Realtime options: 1) force kernel back to fp16-v1 for eu-west serving pool via fw flag 2) route affected traffic to eu-central fallback pool 3) throttle low-priority tenants so critical routes stay within SLO. Which do we want now?

theo_oncall: Do the quick fix: flip kernel flag for the specific node set (not global). We'll coordinate rollout. Also open spike comms to customers if we expect >15m.

maya_ml: Agreed. Suggested command: `redwoodctl featureflag set runtime.kernel.force.fp16-v1 --selector region=eu-west --expires 30m`

erin_runtime: Running that now on the 6 impacted pods. `redwoodctl` output:```
apply featureflag runtime.kernel.force.fp16-v1 to selector region=eu-west: success (6 pods)
```

deploy-bot: Rollout started: fd1a2b -> featureflag/runtime.kernel.force.fp16-v1 targeted to region=eu-west by erin_runtime

aisha_sre: Also enabled transient routing fallback for tenant-affinity route rule for critical workspace_ids. Config: `route.policy=latency_first; fallback=eu-central`

jason_perf: Re-ran short profiler after flag: matmul_kern_fp16_v2 no longer used; fp16_v1 matmul now 0.95ms. KV miss-rate still elevated (0.12 -> 0.15) but queue_wait and tail latencies falling.

erin_runtime: P95 dropped back toward baseline in the last 30s. Monitoring shows slow decay of KV cache misses -- likely due to earlier evictions.

maya_ml: For the medium term, we'll: 1) reproduce locally with same driver/device, 2) add a guard in kernel-selector to avoid fp16-v2 on these driver versions, 3) add a perf regression alert tied to matmul median > 1.5ms.

jason_perf: I'll file PERF-983 and attach traces. Also adding an automatic rollback rule: if p95 increases >1.5x within 5m after kernel swap, revert selector for the bundle.

oliver_ops: Throttling plan: apply route rule `priority=low -> 20rps cap` for non-critical tenants in eu-west for 10m to speed cache warmup. Doing now.

incident-bot: Update INC-2026-0456: mitigations applied (featureflag rollback, routing fallback, tenant throttling). Monitoring.

theo_oncall: Good job. Postmortem owners: @jason_perf (root cause analysis / perf regression), @maya_ml (kernel-selector guards), @oliver_ops (runbook updates). ETA initial postmortem draft 48h.

erin_runtime: Quick note for follow-ups: collect full perf traces from impacted pods, save kernel binaries, include driver versions, and annotate which tenants saw higher miss-rate. I'll upload artifacts to the incident ticket.

maya_ml: Also add a model variant fallback in routing that maps heavy-token models to a more cache-friendly quantized variant while we diagnose. Low-risk change.

jason_perf: Thanks all. Will push PERF-983 and link traces in INC-2026-0456. :thumbsup:
